title: Larkspur Closing Cost Credit Application Against Nonrecurring Closing Costs
content:
**Larkspur Closing Cost Credit — application on the day of the scheduled closing**

On the day of the scheduled closing, while the loan file is clear to close and its Closing Disclosure has been issued, each verified credit on the file is applied on that Closing Disclosure in the order and up to the limits of the combination rules for credits on one loan file, against its nonrecurring closing costs, its discount points, the buydown subsidy of a buydown on the file and, where allowed, its down payment, the application entries being booked that day ahead of the signing. Prepaid items are paid by credits only on the disbursement date, out of whatever balance remains, because prepaid interest and the initial escrow deposit are final only when the loan funds.

For a Larkspur Neighborhood Access Grant the closing-cost entry is one application entry naming that Closing Disclosure and the award entry it draws on.

A Neighborhood Access Grant's closing-cost entry is booked only after the grant stands verified with an award entry on its ledger. Put the other way, while the grant does not stand verified with an award entry on its ledger, no closing-cost entry is booked for it.

| Timing | What credits pay |
|---|---|
| Day of the scheduled closing, file clear to close, Closing Disclosure issued — booked ahead of the signing | nonrecurring closing costs, discount points, the buydown subsidy of a buydown on the file and, where allowed, the down payment |
| Disbursement date, out of whatever balance remains | prepaid items |

### Situation of use and effect of the tool

`post_closing_cost_credit_e81a44da` books the part of a verified closing cost credit that pays the borrower's nonrecurring closing costs on a Closing Disclosure. One call books one application entry for the nonrecurring closing costs category against the named Closing Disclosure, drawing on the named award entry of the same credit, and lowers the credit's available balance by the amount booked. Afterwards the credit's ledger shows the closing cost application entry and the reduced available balance.

### How it is invoked

It is an agent-side tool: the agent unlocks `post_closing_cost_credit_e81a44da` and then calls it.

### Parameters

| Parameter | Meaning | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `credit_award_id` | Reference number of the verified closing cost credit being applied, as shown by the closing credit lookup for the loan file. | An identifier, as shown in the lookup. |
| `disclosure_id` | Reference number of the Closing Disclosure whose nonrecurring closing costs are paid, as shown by the loan disclosure lookup for the same loan file. | An identifier, as shown in the lookup. |
| `source_entry_id` | Reference number of the award entry on this credit's ledger that the application draws on, as shown by the credit ledger lookup for the credit. | An identifier, as shown in the lookup. |
| `entry_amount` | Amount of the credit applied to nonrecurring closing costs. | US dollars as a plain positive number with exactly 2 decimal places (cents), no currency sign or thousands separators; stored as given, rounded to 2 decimal places. |

### Return

> Closing cost application <entry_id> booked: <amount> of credit <credit_award_id> on disclosure <disclosure_id>; available balance <balance>.

<entry_id> is the reference number of the new application entry; <amount> and <balance> are US dollars with 2 decimals. Receiving this line means the application is on the credit's ledger; the call has succeeded when the receipt is returned.
